{"results":[{"key":"session-summary/2026-10-02-review-lines-floor-migration-fixes","value":"re-cinq/lore PR #2444 (branch fix/review-lines-floor-migration, OPEN at time of writing): three defects in the review lines on the external floor, found while comparing the pipeline with QuintinBotes/review-voice.

1. RE-CHECK RANGE. judgedRange (libs/shared/src/work/review/floor-review-start.ts) named the head sha of the NEWEST review-family run in any state as "the last verdict judged". Push B then push C before B's re-check finished: B's run was cancelled as superseded and C's re-check read only B..C, so A..B was never reviewed and that verdict feeds auto-merge. Fix: lastJudgedSha(runs) in floor-review-runs.ts = head_sha of the newest code-review/code-review-recheck run with outcome "success" (the only state where post-review posted). No posted verdict means no range, so the re-check reads the whole PR. Cost accepted: a push while the first deep review is still open now gets a whole-PR re-check.

2. REPLIES NEVER IN-THREAD. post-reply read brief.needs.comment_id, which nothing supplied (a run is started per review, which holds many line comments). Every reply was a top-level PR comment, no thread resolved. Production evidence: lore#2221 (09-28) and HALEngine#99 (09-29) replies are both top-level; no reply has run at all since the 09-30 floor move. Fix: the agent emits an optional REVIEW_THREAD_REPLIES JSON block [{comment_id, reply, resolved}] beside REVIEW_REPLY (parser in libs/shared/src/work/review/review-reply.ts); post-reply takes review_id as a need, posts each entry under its comment only when the comment belongs to that review, replies against in_reply_to_id (the thread's first comment; GitHub accepts a reply only there; ReviewComment gained in_reply_to_id), resolves only threads marked resolved from one listing, folds a stray or GitHub-refused reply into the general comment (so a refused thread does not fail the visit and re-run the agent), and uses a per-comment marker lore-reply-run: visit/iteration/commentId for redelivery.

3. REPLY PROMPT PROMISED MISSING INPUTS. It said the task line states "the intent and the thread"; the task line is review_feedback only. intent was hard-coded "address" and never reached the agent. intent is deleted from startReply, the pipeline args and both stations; the prompt now tells the agent to decide per comment (change, answer, or ask its own question).

DEPLOY NOTE: lore-api seeds the pipeline, stations start the runs; until both deploy, a reply start can be refused because the old pipeline still requires intent.

NOT DONE (ideas from review-voice, features not fixes): a verifier pass that rejects unproven findings before post-review; dropping re-check findings that repeat earlier threads (the re-check is given no earlier findings); an untrusted-input rule in the review prompts (none exists, and the pod can write org memory, the reply pod can push; see #2348); filtering lock/generated files from the reviewed diff; a word limit and banned hedging phrases enforced in post-review. review-voice itself: a 2-week-old single-author Claude Code plugin; its per-reviewer precedent learning has no data behind it by its own EVALUATION.md.

# ADR-039: Cross-model review for agent-authored changes

This ADR proposes that the review node of every assembly line that reviews
agent-authored code run on a different model family than the model that
authored the change, to counter self-preference bias.

> **Where the reviewer's model is set now (2026-10-02).** The code-review lines
> moved to the external floor ([ADR-049](./ADR-049-external-floor.md)). The
> reviewer's model is the `model` of the agent definition inside each floor
> pipeline file (`libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/code-review.yaml`,
> `code-review-recheck.yaml`, `code-review-reply.yaml`), `claude-sonnet-4-6`
> on all three since 2026-10-08, when the implementation loop moved to
> `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, and no longer a `lore.agent_definitions` row. `task-types.yaml`
> and `libs/assembly-lines/src/assembly-lines/code-review.yaml`, both named
> below, are gone. The proposal is unchanged; where it says to pin the review
> default, the place to pin it is those files.

## Decision

The org-default `agent_definitions` row for review-type agents pins a model
from a different family than the implementation default. Concretely: while
the implementation default resolves to the Anthropic/Claude family, the
review default is pinned to OpenAI's current flagship (`gpt-5.6` at time of
writing), and vice versa. When an implementation task's model is overridden
per-repo, the repo owner is responsible for keeping the review model
cross-family; the settings UI surfaces a warning when implementer and
reviewer resolve to the same family.

**Prerequisites.** The ai-agent-subsystem's `claude-code` vendor only calls
the Anthropic API today, so cross-provider review is not yet reachable by
row edits alone: the subsystem needs a second vendor (e.g. `openai-code`)
that runs the review prompt against the OpenAI API and emits the same
`REVIEW_RESULT` marker the node contract parses. That vendor is scoped as a
follow-up to ADR-031. Until it exists, the interim config-only step is a
*different Anthropic model tier* for review — weaker against family-level
self-preference, but immediately available through the resolve chain.

The end state introduces no new mechanism: the policy is expressed entirely
through existing `agent_definitions` rows and their resolve chain.
